name: Cape Town
tagline: Table Mountain, two oceans and the winelands at its feet.
whenBlurb: November to March is the warm, dry summer for the mountain, beaches and Winelands harvest; pair it with whale season on the coast from June, and avoid the wet, windy winter in the city itself.

ourTake.lede: Watch the mountain, not the clock, Table Mountain and Cape Point are worth doing on the first clear, wind-free morning you get, because the cloud and the southeaster can shut them for days. Base half your stay in town and half out on the winelands or the Cape Peninsula; the two feel like different holidays. The Cape Winelands do a private cellar lunch better than almost anywhere, so build a slow day around one estate rather than rushing four.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a mountain-meets-ocean city, world-class wine and safari within reach.
ourTake.skipIf: You want to wander freely at night without watching your surroundings.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Ellerman House
credentials: Travel + Leisure World's Best Awards 2024, Best City Hotel in Africa
items.description: A private cliff-side mansion above the Atlantic, run as a home with one of Africa's great art and wine cellars.

items.name: Mount Nelson, A Belmond Hotel
credentials: World's 50 Best Hotels 2024 (No. 28), Best Hotel in Africa
items.description: The Pink Lady, Cape Town's grande dame since 1899, in nine acres of gardens below Table Mountain.

items.name: One&Only Cape Town
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards 2024
items.description: A marina-side resort with Table Mountain framed in the glass and a private spa island of its own.

items.name: The Silo Hotel
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards
items.description: A converted grain silo crowned with faceted glass, sitting atop the Zeitz MOCAA contemporary-art museum.

items.name: Delaire Graff Lodge
items.description: Laurence Graff's jewel of a wine estate on the Helshoogte Pass, art, diamonds and vineyards at altitude.

items.name: Cape Grace, A Fairmont Managed Hotel
credentials: Travel + Leisure World's Best Awards 2024 (Top City Hotels in Africa, No. 3)
items.description: A warm, quietly grand harbour house on its own quay, with one of the city's finest whisky bars.

items.name: The Cellars-Hohenort
items.description: A country-house hotel in nine acres of Constantia gardens, the calm, green, old-Cape antidote to the city.

items.name: The Twelve Apostles Hotel and Spa
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Triple Crown (Hot List, Gold List & Readers' Choice)
Red Carnation Hotels, TripAdvisor Hall of Fame
items.description: A sea-facing house between mountain and Atlantic on the scenic road to Camps Bay, remote calm, minutes from town.

items.name: Leeu Estates
items.description: A restored Cape Dutch homestead in its own vineyards, the anchor of the Leeu Collection in the valley.

items.name: Steenberg Hotel & Spa
items.description: The Cape's oldest wine farm turned polished retreat, vineyards, a golf course and Cape Dutch calm.

items.name: La Residence
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards 2024 (Top 15 Hotels in South Africa)
items.description: The Royal Portfolio's flamboyant, art-filled manor on a private vine-and-olive estate in the valley.

items.name: Leeu House
items.description: An intimate boutique house in the heart of Franschhoek village, art, gardens and the main street at the door.

items.name: The Last Word Franschhoek
items.description: A small, personal boutique retreat with a garden and mountain views a short stroll from the village.

items.name: Le Quartier Français
items.description: A legendary village inn reborn, the beating heart of Franschhoek's dining-and-village life.

items.name: Akademie Street Boutique Hotel
items.description: A cluster of restored village cottages and suites with private pools, run with real warmth.

items.name: Taj Cape Town
items.description: The old Reserve Bank turned grand city hotel, and the address that speaks Hindi at the door.

items.name: Cape Cadogan Boutique Hotel
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Readers' Choice Awards (Best Hotels in Africa, No. 5)
items.description: A restored Georgian-and-Victorian townhouse on a leafy Gardens street, a calm, characterful city base.

items.name: Table Mountain Aerial Cableway
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cape Floral Region Protected Areas
items.description: The flat-topped mountain that defines Cape Town's skyline, reached in five minutes by a cable car with a slowly rotating floor so every passenger gets the full 360-degree sweep of the city, Table Bay and the Twelve Apostles. Book the earliest morning slot with your guide before the wind picks up (the cableway closes in high wind), and the summit walks stay gentle enough for grandparents and children alike.

items.name: Platteklip Gorge Hike up Table Mountain
items.description: The direct, non-technical route straight up the mountain's front face, a steep two-to-three hour climb rewarded with the same summit views and the option to ride the cableway back down. A private mountain guide is worth it for pacing, safety and the geology and fynbos along the way.

items.name: Cape Point & the Cape of Good Hope
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cape Floral Region Protected Areas
items.description: The dramatic rocky headland at the south-western tip of the peninsula, with a funicular to the old lighthouse and cliff paths above the meeting of two great oceans. It sits inside a nature reserve full of eland, bontebok and cheeky baboons, and pairs naturally with a full private-driver day looping the peninsula.

items.name: Chapman's Peak Drive
items.description: A 9-kilometre toll road carved into a sheer cliff face between Hout Bay and Noordhoek, counted among the world's great coastal drives with 114 curves hanging above the Atlantic. Ask your driver to stop at the lookouts for photographs; it is glorious at golden hour on the way back from Cape Point.

items.name: Boulders Beach Penguin Colony
credentials: Part of Table Mountain National Park
items.description: A sheltered cove of granite boulders near Simon's Town that is home to a colony of African penguins you can watch from boardwalks just metres away, the only place in the world you get this close on a mainland beach. An easy, delightful stop for children and a rare wildlife encounter that needs no effort.

items.name: Kirstenbosch National Botanical Garden
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cape Floral Region Protected Areas
items.description: One of the great botanical gardens of the world, spread across the eastern slopes of Table Mountain and dedicated to the Cape's extraordinary indigenous flora. The 130-metre Boomslang canopy walkway lifts you into the treetops, and summer sunset concerts on the lawns are a civilised, family-friendly evening with a picnic hamper.

items.name: V&A Waterfront
items.description: A working harbour reinvented as Cape Town's most polished precinct, with luxury shopping, waterside restaurants, the Two Oceans Aquarium and the ferry gateway to Robben Island. Safe to stroll after dark, well suited to a multi-generation base, and a comfortable anchor for the whole trip.

items.name: Zeitz MOCAA
credentials: Largest museum of contemporary African art in the world
items.description: Africa's largest museum of contemporary art, carved by Heatherwick Studio out of a historic grain silo in the Waterfront's Silo District across nine sculpted floors. Even non-art-lovers linger over the architecture, and the sixth-floor rooftop terrace frames Table Mountain and the harbour.

items.name: Robben Island Museum
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Robben Island
items.description: The island prison where Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years, reached by ferry from the Waterfront and toured by former political prisoners who lived the history they narrate. A moving, essential half-day; book well ahead as tours sell out, and it gives older children real context for South Africa's story.

items.name: Bo-Kaap
items.description: The historic heart of Cape Malay culture on the slopes of Signal Hill, famous for cobbled lanes of vivid, hand-painted houses and the oldest mosque in South Africa. A private walking tour with a resident, ending in a Cape Malay cooking session, resonates especially with Indian travellers for its shared spice heritage and largely vegetarian-friendly kitchen.

items.name: Bo-Kaap Museum
items.description: Set in the oldest surviving house in the quarter, this small Iziko museum tells the story of the Muslim settlers, exiles and skilled artisans who shaped the neighbourhood. A quiet, thoughtful counterpoint to the colourful streets outside.

items.name: Company's Garden
items.description: The oldest garden in the country, laid out by the Dutch East India Company in the 1650s to grow produce for passing ships and now a leafy central park lined with museums, oak avenues and a heritage rose garden. A gentle, shaded stroll in the middle of the city, ringed by the national museums and galleries.

items.name: Iziko South African Museum & Planetarium
items.description: The country's oldest museum, strong on natural history, San rock art and the whale gallery, with a digital planetarium under the same roof. An easy, air-conditioned option for a hot afternoon and genuinely engaging for children.

items.name: Signal Hill
items.description: A drive-up ridge above the city delivering one of the finest sunset panoramas over the Atlantic, Sea Point and Lion's Head, with no climb required. Ideal for grandparents or an easy evening; arrive with your driver well before the sun drops for the best spot.

items.name: The Noon Gun
items.description: A cannon on Signal Hill's lower slopes that has been fired at midday almost every day since 1806, once helping ships set their chronometers. A quirky ritual best paired with the walk up through the Bo-Kaap that leads to it.

items.name: Lion's Head Hike
items.description: A spiralling 5.5-kilometre round-trip climb with chains and ladders near the top, delivering a 360-degree summit view of city, sea and Table Mountain. Fit travellers do it at sunrise or full moon with a guide; not one for the very young or those unsure of heights.

items.name: Camps Bay Beach
items.description: Cape Town's glamorous beachfront, a wide white-sand bay backed by the Twelve Apostles and a strip of stylish restaurants and bars. The ocean is bracingly cold but the palm-lined promenade, sundowners and people-watching make it the address for a relaxed afternoon.

items.name: Clifton Beaches
items.description: Four sheltered coves separated by granite outcrops, the most exclusive stretch of sand in the city and protected from the wind that troubles other beaches. Fourth Beach flies a Blue Flag; bring a hamper and settle in for a discreet, upmarket beach day.

items.name: Groot Constantia
credentials: Oldest wine estate in South Africa (est. 1685)
items.description: The oldest wine estate in South Africa, founded in 1685, with a beautifully preserved Cape Dutch manor, a wine museum and cellar tours 20 minutes from the city. Its historic Grand Constance dessert wine once graced European royal tables and Napoleon's exile; tastings on the lawn suit an unhurried family lunch.

items.name: Klein Constantia
items.description: A boutique estate on the Constantia slopes reviving the legendary Vin de Constance, the sweet wine adored by kings, emperors and Jane Austen's characters alike. An elegant, less-crowded tasting with valley-and-sea views, ideal for the discerning collector.

items.name: Buitenverwachting
items.description: A gracious wine estate on the Constantia route, prized as much for its oak-shaded picnic lawns and fine-dining restaurant as its wines. A calm, green afternoon close to the city, with a kitchen that will happily accommodate vegetarian preferences on notice.

items.name: Steenberg Vineyards
items.description: The oldest farm in the Constantia valley, now a polished estate known for its Méthode Cap Classique sparkling wines, a modern tasting room and an acclaimed restaurant. Golf, a boutique hotel and vineyard views make it a refined base or day-stop.

items.name: Stellenbosch Winelands
items.description: The country's second-oldest town, an easy 45 minutes from the city, with oak-lined streets of Cape Dutch architecture and hundreds of estates around it. A private-driver day here means unhurried cellar visits, world-class lunches and no one at the wheel counting their tastings.

items.name: Franschhoek Wine Tram
items.description: A hop-on-hop-off double-decker tram and open tram-bus that wanders between the historic estates of the Franschhoek valley, letting you taste at your own pace without a designated driver. Franschhoek is the Cape's gastronomic capital, and the whole day feels leisurely and multi-generational.

items.name: Babylonstoren
items.description: A spectacular working farm and estate near Franschhoek built around one of the great formal gardens of the world, with farm-to-table dining, wine, a spa and a hotel. A full immersive day; the produce-driven kitchens are a joy for vegetable-forward and vegetarian tables.

items.name: Delaire Graff Estate
items.description: A hilltop estate on the Helshoogte Pass owned by the diamond house Graff, pairing serious wine with a sculpture collection, two restaurants and a lodge over the Stellenbosch valley. The definition of discreet Winelands luxury and a natural fit for high-net-worth travellers.

items.name: Boschendal Wine Estate
items.description: One of the oldest farms between Stellenbosch and Franschhoek, with a Manor House, farm shop, deli picnics under the oaks and family-friendly grounds. Relaxed and beautiful, and easy for children and grandparents to enjoy alongside the wine.

items.name: Hermanus Whale Watching
items.description: A clifftop town about 90 minutes from the city offering some of the best land-based whale watching in the world, with southern right whales calving metres from the Walker Bay shore between roughly June and November. Boat cruises get you closer still; a magical seasonal day-trip, gentle enough for all ages.

items.name: Shark Cage Diving, Gansbaai
items.description: About two hours from the city, the waters off Gansbaai near 'Shark Alley' draw great whites and copper sharks to a huge Cape fur seal colony. Reputable operators lower you in a surface cage; a bucket-list thrill for adventurous members, with viewing-only from the boat for those who prefer to stay dry.

items.name: Two Oceans Aquarium
items.description: A well-run aquarium at the Waterfront showcasing the marine life where the cold Atlantic meets the warmer Indian Ocean, with a kelp forest, ragged-tooth sharks and a penguin exhibit. A reliable, weather-proof hit for children and an easy add-on to a Waterfront day.

items.name: Hout Bay & Seal Island Cruise
items.description: A working fishing harbour ringed by mountains, from where short boat trips run out to Duiker Island's noisy Cape fur seal colony. Combine it with the craft market and a seafood lunch; it slots neatly into the Chapman's Peak route.

items.name: Oranjezicht City Farm Market
items.description: The city's finest farmers' market, held weekends at Granger Bay on the Waterfront, with more than a hundred producers of organic produce, artisanal food and pastries under the mountain. A superb, safe morning of grazing with plenty of vegetarian and vegan stalls.

items.name: Neighbourgoods Market at the Old Biscuit Mill
items.description: The market that launched Cape Town's food-market scene, held Saturdays in a converted mill in Woodstock and buzzing with street food, design and music. Go with a guide or driver and go early; it is lively, creative and best enjoyed at a relaxed pace.

items.name: Langa Township Cultural Tour
items.description: The oldest formal township in Cape Town, best visited on a respectful, community-led tour that takes in the Guga S'Thebe arts centre, local homes and the living history of the apartheid era. Choose an operator that channels spending back into the community for an honest, humanising counterpoint to the city's postcard views.

items.name: District Six Museum
items.description: A deeply affecting community museum remembering the vibrant multiracial district whose residents were forcibly removed and homes bulldozed under apartheid. Small but powerful, and the single best half-hour for understanding the human cost behind Cape Town's beauty.

items.name: Muizenberg Beach
items.description: A gentle, warmer False Bay beach famous for its row of candy-coloured Victorian bathing boxes and forgiving waves, the classic place for a first surf lesson. Family-friendly and photogenic, and a natural stop on the peninsula loop.

items.name: Cape Town City Centre & The Fringe / St George's Mall
items.description: The compact old town rewards a guided walk past Greenmarket Square's craft stalls, Church Street's antiques and Cape Dutch and Art Deco facades. Best explored on foot with a guide by day for the architecture, history and coffee culture.

items.name: The Castle of Good Hope
credentials: Oldest surviving colonial building in South Africa
items.description: The oldest surviving colonial building in South Africa, a star-shaped Dutch fort completed in 1679, now home to military and art collections and a daily key ceremony. A concise dose of the Cape's founding history for those who like their landmarks tangible.

items.name: Sea Point Promenade
items.description: A broad, flat seaside walkway running for kilometres along the Atlantic, dotted with public art, lawns and a tidal pool, and busy with strollers, joggers and families at sunset. Level and safe, it suits everyone from toddlers to grandparents.

items.name: Constantia Valley Cycle or Manor Walk
items.description: The leafy Constantia valley invites a gentle guided cycle or garden walk between historic estates, all within 20 minutes of the city. A relaxed, green half-day that families can pace to their own comfort.

items.name: West Coast National Park & Spring Flowers
items.description: About 90 minutes north, the Postberg section of this park erupts into carpets of wildflowers each August and September, around the turquoise Langebaan lagoon. A stunning seasonal drive with wildlife and birdlife, easy and rewarding for all ages.

items.name: Twelve Apostles & Bakoven Sundowners
items.description: The buttress of peaks running south from Table Mountain forms the backdrop to the Atlantic seaboard's most cinematic sunsets, best watched from a terrace or the rocks at Bakoven. A quietly luxurious way to close a Cape Town day.

items.name: Silo District & Waterfront Art Walk
items.description: Beyond Zeitz MOCAA, the Silo precinct and wider Waterfront hold a growing cluster of galleries, design stores and public sculpture in a safe, walkable setting. An unhurried cultural afternoon that dovetails with harbour dining.

items.name: Table Mountain National Park Fynbos Walks
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cape Floral Region Protected Areas
items.description: Beyond the summit, the park's lower trails at Silvermine, Cape Point and Kirstenbosch let you walk through the Cape Floral Kingdom, the richest and most concentrated plant kingdom on earth. A private botanical guide turns a gentle walk into a revelation for nature-minded travellers.

items.name: Cape Malay Cooking Experience
items.description: A hands-on private class in a Bo-Kaap home teaching the spice-laden Cape Malay dishes, bobotie, samoosas, breyani, that carry echoes of Indian and Indonesian kitchens. A warm, intimate cultural exchange that vegetarian travellers can readily tailor.

items.name: La Colombe
credentials: World's 50 Best Restaurants No. 49 (2024), Best Restaurant in Africa
items.description: Cape Town's most celebrated kitchen, a treehouse-like room above Silvermist, and Africa's benchmark for fine dining.

items.name: FYN
credentials: Eat Out Restaurant of the Year & Three Stars (2026)
items.description: Japanese precision married to South African produce, the only stand-alone African restaurant in Relais & Châteaux.

items.name: Salsify at the Roundhouse
credentials: Eat Out Restaurant of the Year & Three Stars (2025)
items.description: Chef Ryan Cole's seasonal cooking in a historic hunting lodge, with the Atlantic sweeping below.

items.name: La Petite Colombe
items.description: La Colombe's Winelands sibling at Leeu Estates, theatrical tasting menus among the vines.

items.name: Pier
items.description: Waterside fine dining with table-side theatre and the ocean's finest produce at its centre.

items.name: Salon
items.description: An intimate, ambitious tasting-menu room that climbed to the very top of the Cape's rankings.

items.name: Dusk
items.description: A Stellenbosch tasting-menu room that arrived at three stars almost fully formed.

items.name: Wolfgat
credentials: World Restaurant Awards, Restaurant of the Year (inaugural)
items.description: Kobus van der Merwe's veldkos, foraged 'field food' from the strandveld, in a fisherman's cottage by the sea.

items.name: Beyond
items.description: Buitenverwachting's elegant estate restaurant, refined cooking among the Constantia vines.

items.name: Chefs Warehouse at Beau Constantia
items.description: Small tapas-style plates on a mountainside deck with one of the Cape's great views.

items.name: Foxcroft
items.description: Refined 'soigné' cooking in an approachable, everyday-elegant Constantia room.

items.name: Ouzeri
items.description: Nic Charalambous's modern Greek-Cypriot, family recipes, Cape produce, and a buzzing Wale Street room.

items.name: The Pot Luck Club
items.description: Luke Dale Roberts's tapas-and-views room atop the Old Biscuit Mill, small plates, big city panorama.

items.name: The Waterside
items.description: Waterside fine dining with a light, produce-led hand and harbour calm.

items.name: Rust en Vrede
items.description: A landmark wine-estate restaurant in a 300-year-old cellar, polished cooking and revered reds.

items.name: Epice
items.description: A spice-led tasting menu in the village, fragrant, considered, and quietly excellent.

items.name: Protégé
items.description: A young-guns village kitchen doing sharp, seasonal cooking without ceremony.

items.name: MERTIA
items.description: A Stellenbosch tasting room that rose to the very top, precise, ingredient-led, personal.

items.name: Belly of the Beast
items.description: One lunch, one dinner, no menu, a daily set feast of local, sustainable produce, cooked with heart.

items.name: Galjoen
items.description: Sustainably caught South African seafood from the Belly of the Beast team, sea-to-table and quietly serious.

items.name: The Test Kitchen Fledgelings
items.description: Luke Dale Roberts's learning kitchen, training the next generation while cooking at a starred level.

items.name: Upper Union
items.description: An intimate neighbourhood room punching well above its size, on the slopes of the City Bowl.

items.name: Chefs Warehouse at Tintswalo Atlantic
items.description: Small plates at the water's edge below the Twelve Apostles, cooking and coastline in equal measure.

items.name: Ëlgr
items.description: A pared-back, produce-first tasting room in the city, quiet, precise, ingredient-led.

items.name: The Red Room by Chefs Warehouse
items.description: The Chefs Warehouse group's intimate city room, small, sharing-led plates done with real polish.

items.name: Le Coin Français
items.description: Classic French technique in the village, from a chef with a devoted following.

items.name: Amura
items.description: Ángel León's Cape Town debut at the Mount Nelson, the 'chef of the sea', translated to the Atlantic.

items.name: Reverie Social Table
items.description: A communal-table neighbourhood favourite where you eat what the chef feels like cooking.

items.name: Chefs Warehouse at Maison
items.description: Small plates and vineyard views at a Franschhoek wine estate, relaxed, generous, sharing-led.

items.name: Willaston Bar
credentials: Within The Silo Hotel, Leading Hotels of the World; The Royal Portfolio
items.description: The Silo Hotel's double-height sixth-floor bar, teal banquettes, circular chandeliers and harbour views, the sheltered counterpart to the rooftop above.

items.name: Bascule Whisky, Wine & Cocktail Bar
credentials: Within Cape Grace, A Fairmont Managed Hotel, MICHELIN Two Keys (2025)
items.description: At Cape Grace on its own quay, more than four hundred whiskies and a marina-side terrace, the city's most serious address for a dram.

items.name: Ellerman House bar & terrace
credentials: Within Ellerman House, Relais & Châteaux; MICHELIN Two Keys (2025)
items.description: Sundowners on a cliff-side lawn above the Atlantic, drawn from a nine-thousand-bottle cellar of South Africa's finest, arguably the most beautiful sundowner in the city.

items.name: Cause | Effect Cocktail Kitchen
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery selection
Home of the Cape Brandy Bar
items.description: Cape Town in a glass, fynbos, brandy and closed-loop, waterless technique from one of the country's most awarded bar teams, at the Waterfront and on Kloof Street.

items.name: Art of Duplicity
credentials: World's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery selection; ranked in the extended World's 50 Best Bars list
items.description: A password-only speakeasy in a Victorian warehouse, velvet, mahogany and one of the city's most inventive cocktail lists, found by those who know to look.

items.name: The Silo Rooftop
credentials: The Silo Hotel, Leading Hotels of the World; MICHELIN One Key (2025)
items.description: Drinks on the roof of the pillowed-glass Silo Hotel, above Zeitz MOCAA, the definitive Cape Town sundowner, Table Mountain on one side, the Atlantic on the other.

items.name: Chinchilla Rooftop
credentials: Named among the world's best rooftop bars; Kove Collection
items.description: Above the Camps Bay strip, the sun going down over the Atlantic, Lion's Head and the Twelve Apostles behind, cocktails and DJs as the beach empties.

items.name: Bree Street
credentials: Cape Town's defining bar-and-restaurant street, City Bowl
items.description: The city's coolest block after dark, wine bars, cocktail haunts and pavement tables strung along a heritage street, the natural place to begin a Cape Town night.

items.name: Long Street
credentials: Cape Town's most famous nightlife street, City Bowl
items.description: The Mother City's historic nightlife spine, Victorian balconies, live music and clubs running till dawn, loud, mixed and unpretentious.

plan.heading: 5 days in Cape Town, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Table Mountain cableway on a clear early morning, then a walk along the upper contour path.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Company's Garden and the Zeitz MOCAA at the V&A Waterfront, housed in the old grain silo.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at La Colombe on the Silvermist estate, or the tasting menu at Fyn in the city.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A drive down Chapman's Peak to Cape Point and the Cape of Good Hope with a private guide.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The penguins at Boulders Beach, then a seafood lunch in Kalk Bay's harbour.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A quiet dinner back in the city at Chef's Warehouse, small plates and Cape wines.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A drive to Franschhoek, tasting at Boschendal and the historic La Motte estate.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at the Michelin-recognised La Petite Colombe, then Delaire Graff for the art and the view.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Stay over at Delaire Graff Lodges, or return for dinner at the Test Kitchen's successor kitchens.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The colour and Cape-Malay history of the Bo-Kaap with a local, then the spice shops.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Constantia wine route, Groot Constantia and Klein Constantia's famed Vin de Constance.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sundowners at Camps Bay, then dinner on the terrace at the Twelve Apostles hotel.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning boat to Robben Island, told by a former inmate as guide.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A slow lunch at The Pot Luck Club in Woodstock, then the design and galleries of the district.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A final dinner at Belmond Mount Nelson's Planet Bar and restaurant, in its pink colonial calm.

items.name: Camps Bay & Clifton
items.description: The Atlantic seaboard of beaches and sunset views beneath the Twelve Apostles; suits those who want sea, glamour and pool days.

items.name: V&A Waterfront & City Bowl
items.description: Central, walkable, close to the museums and the mountain cableway; best for first-timers who want everything at hand.

items.name: Constantia
items.description: Leafy, low-rise wine country within the city, with historic estates and space; for a calm, green base near the vineyards.

events.name: Cape Town Minstrel Carnival (Kaapse Klopse)
events.note: The city's oldest carnival, thousands of costumed minstrels with banjos and ghoema drums parade through the streets.

events.name: Cape Town International Jazz Festival
events.note: Africa's grandest jazz gathering, two days of local and international acts across multiple stages at the CTICC.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in Camps Bay, Clifton, or the V&A Waterfront; book Table Mountain and Robben Island around the weather, keep valuables discreet, and reserve Winelands lunches (Delaire, Boschendal) ahead.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Cape Town International (CPT); a private chauffeur handles the 20–30 minute drive to the Atlantic Seaboard, or a helicopter transfer for a first sight of Table Mountain.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver-guide is the way to move between the city, the Cape Peninsula, and the Winelands; the V&A Waterfront and Camps Bay are walkable in themselves.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: eSIM (Vodacom, MTN) is excellent; note scheduled power cuts (loadshedding) can affect signal and wifi, though top hotels run full backup power.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The South African rand (ZAR) is the currency; cards are accepted everywhere, keep some cash for markets and guides, and 10–15% is the standard tip.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: November-March is Cape Town's summer, warm, dry, long days, Table Mountain and the winelands at their peak; June-August is the wet, windy winter and best avoided for a first visit.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No nonstop from India; the best routings are one stop via Doha on Qatar Airways or via Addis Ababa on Ethiopian, roughly 15-17 hours total. Qatar via Doha gives the strongest business product and the Al Mourjan lounge; the Doha-Cape Town leg is about 10 hours, so an angled-flat or better seat matters.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No special vaccinations beyond routine; hepatitis A worth being current on. Cape Town itself is malaria-free (Kruger/lowveld add-ons are not, take precautions there). Tap water is safe to drink. Safe in the tourist and winelands areas, but crime exists, use trusted drivers, avoid walking at night, and don't display valuables.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Strong for vegetarians, Cape Town has a serious plant-forward dining scene; Jain is workable with briefing. Indian and Cape Malay food is excellent and widely available; for refined vegetarian, the top Constantia and city restaurants cater well, and Cape Malay curries offer genuinely good meat-free options.
